subject: Next steps: technical deep-dive + evaluation kickoff for Healthlytics
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Barnes <tbarnes@healthlytics.com>, Amy Zhou <amy.z@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: technical deep-dive + evaluation kickoff for Healthlytics

Hi Timothy / Amy —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through where you’re seeing latency spikes in the nightly batch and the variability in per-request costs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

High-level recap from discovery:
- Primary goals: reduce inference tail latency for customer-facing queries, and stabilize token cost for the nightly ETL scoring job.
- Constraints: SOC2/PII controls, on-prem gateway for PHI-sensitive data, 99th-pct latency target ~200ms for web queries.
- Stakeholders: Timothy (product/ops), Amy (data eng), ops-team@healthlytics.com (platform)

Proposed next meeting: 60–75 minute technical deep-dive + evaluation kickoff where we will:
1) Demo model routing & tracing (how we surface per-request latency/cost).
2) Walk through a 4-week trial plan (objectives, success criteria, evaluation prompts, telemetry to collect).
3) Align on a mutual action plan and calendar for prompt set uploads / access.

Avl slots (PST):
- Tue 16 Mar, 10:00–11:15am
- Wed 17 Mar, 2:00–3:15pm (preferred for our infra folks)
- Thu 18 Mar, 9:00–10:15am

Please reply with the best slot and any other folks you’d like on the call (engineers, infra). Also: can you share 5 representative prompts or a small prompt file (no PHI) you’d like us to run during the trial? If you prefer, we can provide a template for prompt collection.

Attaching a draft trial plan and a prompt-sample file to help you review before the kickoff: [Attachment: Healthlytics_Redwood_TrialPlan_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)], [Attachment: healthlytics_prompt_samples.jsonl (1.8KB)].

If it helps, I’ll open a HubSpot deal record and a shared Drive folder for drop-in artifacts.

Thanks — I’ll loop Vivek and Neha for scheduling and success-criteria alignment.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — inference for production (redwood.com)

From: Timothy Barnes <tbarnes@healthlytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Amy Zhou <amy.z@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: technical deep-dive + evaluation kickoff for Healthlytics

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. Wednesday 17 Mar 2:00pm PT works best for us (Amy and I can make that).

We’ll invite one of our infra engineers (ops-team@healthlytics.com) to join. I’ll pull together 5 example prompts (non-PHI) and drop them into the shared Drive link you create.

Two quick clarifications:
1) The nightly ETL job runs at 01:30 PT and uses sequences up to ~2k tokens — will you need a sample of that traffic or is representative short prompts enough for initial perf estimates?
2) On data residency: we need an outline of what stays in our VPC vs what would hit Redwood-hosted telemetry during a trial.

Appreciate it — see you Wed.

—Tim

Perfect — locking Wed 17 Mar 2:00–3:15pm PT. Invite will come from Vivek (below).

To answer Timothy’s questions quickly:
- For initial perf estimates a representative short prompt set is fine; for a focused ETL/throughput pass we’ll want a small sample of the 2k-token sequences (we can keep it redacted). Either way, please don’t include PHI in the sample uploads.
- Regarding telemetry/residency: we’ll include a short data flow slide in the kickoff that shows what telemetry is optional vs required. In short: model inputs can be routed through your VPC (Private deployment) during the trial; if you use our hosted route we’ll only persist anonymized logs required for metrics unless you opt in to share traces. We’ll confirm exact controls during the kickoff.

Neha — could you prep the success-criteria checklist and a minimal prompt-template we can send to Healthlytics before Wed? Vivek — can you send the calendar invite and include the shared Drive + HubSpot link?

Thanks all — I’ll stand by for the invite.

Jasmine

Hi Timothy / Amy —

Calendar invite: Wed, 17 Mar 2027, 2:00–3:15pm PT (Google Meet link included in invite). Please accept if that slot works and add any engineers to the event.

Quick attachments and plan highlights (attached):
- Healthlytics_Redwood_TrialPlan_v1.pdf — 4-week trial with weekly milestones, telemetry to collect, and roles/responsibilities.
- healthlytics_prompt_samples.jsonl — a tiny non-PHI prompt set (5 prompts) to run a quick smoke test in the kickoff.

Success criteria (draft checklist):
- 99th-pct web-query latency <= 200ms under baseline traffic (measured via trace samples)
- Nightly ETL throughput with avg per-token cost reduction >= 15% vs current baseline
- No PII/PHI leakage confirmed via our scan tool during trial
- Observability: per-route latency + per-token cost surfaced in Redwood Console for the trial set

Immediate asks from Healthlytics before Wed:
1) Upload the 5 representative prompts (or confirm you’ll use our template).
2) Provide a redacted sample of 1–2 longer sequences (~2k tokens) if you want a throughput run in week 2.
3) Confirm the names/emails of any platform engineers who should be on the kickoff.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HLT-2027-467
Shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-healthlytics-eval

Attachments (stubs): [Attachment: Healthlytics_Redwood_TrialPlan_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)], [Attachment: healthlytics_prompt_samples.jsonl (JSONL, 1.8KB)]

If that looks good I’ll also post the success-criteria checklist into the Drive so you can comment inline.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
